title: Minimum Flips for Palindromic Grid
description:
You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid` containing only `0`s and `1`s.

A row or column is considered **palindromic** if its values read the same forward and backward. In a single operation, you may flip any cell (`0` to `1`, or `1` to `0`).

Return the minimum number of flips required so that **either** all rows are palindromic **or** all columns are palindromic.
hints: Making all rows palindromic and making all columns palindromic are independent goals; compute both costs and take the minimum.
To make a row palindromic, count symmetric pairs (c, n - 1 - c) that differ—each differing pair requires exactly 1 flip.

examples.explanation: Flipping two cells makes all rows palindromic, whereas making all columns palindromic requires 3 flips; the minimum is 2.
Flipping just cell (2, 1) makes both columns palindromic in 1 flip, while rows need 2 flips.
Every single-element row (and column) is already palindromic, needing 0 flips.
